subject.title: [Security] Missing input sanitization on user-supplied webhook endpoint URLs

question: Does a current OpenClaw webhook or outbound delivery path let a non-trusted party influence a non-HTTP(S) endpoint and produce impact beyond the trusted-operator configuration model?
rationale: The documented configuration contract and security policy do not establish the claimed auto-reply path or a boundary bypass, while an actual exploit report must be handled privately.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Ask the reporter to submit a GitHub Security Advisory with the exact config key, current version, request trace, and demonstrated impact before assigning implementation work.

options.title: Confirm and repair
options.body: If the advisory proves an operator-independent bypass, assign the owning outbound/config path for strict scheme validation and regression tests.

options.title: Close as unsupported
options.body: If no current path or boundary-bypass evidence is provided, close the public report without changing broad webhook policy.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask the reporter to submit a GitHub Security Advisory with the exact config key, current version, request trace, and demonstrated impact before assigning implementation work.
